read_only_option.read_receipts: persisted as usual; read-only refers to management operations
read_only_option.project_scope: all projects in the selected library; task metadata is retained for local read-receipt correlation only and does not restrict access

not_permitted: modify a manuscript's bytes in place; updates are new retained baselines
publish an author decision: the storage rules refuse agent proposals by design
register page-evidence render bundles: independent human evidence goes through the operator CLI or browser
infer page coordinates or page mappings
read content that discovery did not disclose
authenticate a remote or multi-user caller
evidence_rules: Every tool delegates to WorkbenchService; the MCP layer holds no separate business rule.
A declared refusal reaches the client with its reason, never as a generic execution failure.
Unknown top-level tool argument names are refused at the MCP boundary before a service operation; the SDK validates declared argument values.

read_objects accepts optional com.oleafly/research-task MCP request metadata containing system, project_id, task_id and generation; Oleafly ResearchTask sends it only to a server identifying as research-file-workbench, for local receipt correlation only, not authentication or project authorization.
With --read-only, management tools are neither advertised nor callable. The default local-operator surface retains all 18 tools.
Discovery records no content read and no review.
A read is recorded as a read receipt; the receipt is the design behaviour, not a mutation.

A world import or revision is the same retained record the browser writes, carrying local-operator as the actor. A manuscript import or update retains a confirmation reason naming the driving surface (browser, mcp or cli); a binding, check or disposition record carries a surface field naming it. World revision records stay actor-attributed only while the retained world schema is frozen.
Coverage stays partial while the reader declares limits.
limits: This is a local single-operator interface. It is not an authenticated remote service.
The desktop shell and this entry point share one library; neither is a second authority.
Authenticated MCP, task-material directories and full S1 independent acceptance remain separate work.
Unknown top-level arguments are checked against the SDK-generated schemas through the SDK's public middleware hook. That hook is provisional within SDK 2.x; real-stdio regression tests cover it.
Nested source records tolerate unknown keys beyond the declared name/kind/content_base64; handlers never use an ignored key.
